text.p: Caspian Securities has reiterated its buy ratings on Brazilian federal telecom holding Telebras and its Minas Gerais state unit Telemig.

-- Caspian analysts Tony Figueiredo and Joanne Showalter said they also maintained their market-performer ratings on Telebras units Telesp and Telerj, serving Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro states respectively.
-- Telebras' decision to distribute shares to subscribers to its 1996 autofinancing program instead of cash was unwelcome news for Telebras shareholders, they said.
-- "We estimate dilution of up to three percent for the shareholders of some of the Telebras subsidiaries, with Telemig shareholders probably faring the best," they wrote.
-- Most lines sold by Telemig last year were through their rental program and not autofinancing, so the number of shares to be issued by the firm should be "insignficant," the analysts said.
-- "In any case, our estimates for Telebras as well as subsidiaries already included an increase in the number of shares, so additional dilution, if any, should be minimal," they added.
-- Telebras' ADR was up 1-7/8 at 151-3/8 in New York while its preferred was up 1.48 percent at 164.90 reais in Sao Paulo at 1447 local/1747 GMT.

-- Telemig common was up 2.33 percent at 176 reais, Telesp preferred was 1.85 percent higher at 385 reais and Telerj common was 0.92 percent higher at 165.51 reais in Sao Paulo at 1448 local/1748 EDT/
